verses.1: A psalm of David. O LORD, hear my prayer; give ear to my plea in your faithfulness, answer me in your righteousness.
verses.2: And do not bring judgment upon your servant, for no living soul is righteous before you.
verses.3: For my enemy has crushed my life to the ground. He has made me sit in darkness like the dead of old.
verses.4: My spirit is wrapped around me; my heart is troubled within me.
verses.5: I have remembered days of old, I have meditated on all your works, on the works of your hands I have pondered.
verses.6: I have stretched out my hands to you; my soul, like a weary land, waits for you. Selah.
verses.7: O LORD, answer me quickly, my spirit fails. Do not hide your face from me, or I will be like those descending into the pit.
verses.8: Let your steadfast love be heard by me in the morning, for in you I have trusted. Show me the path I must walk, for to you I have lifted up my soul.
verses.9: Deliver me, O LORD, from my enemies. To you I have taken refuge.
verses.10: Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good spirit will guide me on even ground.
verses.11: For the sake of your name, O LORD, preserve my life in your righteousness. Bring my soul out of distress.
verses.12: And by your steadfast love you will destroy my enemies, and you will make all who afflict my life perish, for I am your servant.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: "Selah" is retained as an untranslated musical or liturgical marker, as is traditional in psalmic texts.
- v. 10: "good spirit" is chosen over "holy spirit" to align with the context of divine guidance and the use of "ruach" in the Hebrew.
raw:
[1] A psalm of David. O LORD, hear my prayer; give ear to my plea in your faithfulness, answer me in your righteousness.

[2] And do not bring judgment upon your servant, for no living soul is righteous before you.

[3] For my enemy has crushed my life to the ground. He has made me sit in darkness like the dead of old.

[4] My spirit is wrapped around me; my heart is troubled within me.

[5] I have remembered days of old, I have meditated on all your works, on the works of your hands I have pondered.

[6] I have stretched out my hands to you; my soul, like a weary land, waits for you. Selah.

[7] O LORD, answer me quickly, my spirit fails. Do not hide your face from me, or I will be like those descending into the pit.

[8] Let your steadfast love be heard by me in the morning, for in you I have trusted. Show me the path I must walk, for to you I have lifted up my soul.

[9] Deliver me, O LORD, from my enemies. To you I have taken refuge.

[10] Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good spirit will guide me on even ground.

[11] For the sake of your name, O LORD, preserve my life in your righteousness. Bring my soul out of distress.

[12] And by your steadfast love you will destroy my enemies, and you will make all who afflict my life perish, for I am your servant.

---

Notes
- v. 6: "Selah" is retained as an untranslated musical or liturgical marker, as is traditional in psalmic texts.
- v. 10: "good spirit" is chosen over "holy spirit" to align with the context of divine guidance and the use of "ruach" in the Hebrew.
